sentences.text: If you stack floors on a sidewalk, you have a pile of blocks.
But all that weight sinks into the soft ground and the stack leans.
So you dig a pit and drive 192 concrete piles down to solid rock.
But the piles stand apart, so you pour a thick concrete mat that ties their tops together and spreads the load over all of them.
This is a piled raft foundation.
Steel columns rise floor by floor, and the piles pass the weight down to the rock.
But now the tall, slim tower catches the wind like a sail and sways from side to side.
So you hang a giant steel weight near the top that swings against the sway and calms it.
And people think thick walls hold a building up, but that is not true, because the frame stands without them.
The steel skeleton carries the load, an idea first used in Chicago in 1885.
Add glass walls, a spire and entrance steps.
Congratulations, you have built a skyscraper.
